_doc: Topics where harness/population_witness.py is VALIDATED on that topic's own families (read from registry criteria, primary report enrolment sentence and title). A topic is used only when listed VALIDATED with a validation record; the protocol's structured B-prime declaration (glp1-ra-mace-t2d) is its own route. comorbidity_only_from_protocol: topics where the protocol's '<X>-only' exclusion wording has been checked to mean 'X without the qualifying condition' (a comorbidity), so those population_none terms exclude only when the qualifying condition is absent.

denosumab-vertebral-fracture.why_population_terms: the topic's population_none also lists drugs (romosozumab, teriparatide, abaloparatide, bisphosphonate) and a procedure (vertebroplasty); read as population exclusions they excluded romosozumab and abaloparatide trials on 'population'

dapagliflozin-hfpef-hosp.check: CARDIA-STIFF NCT04739215 requires T2D + LVEF >= 50% + clinically diagnosed HFpEF: a comorbidity, not a diabetes-only population

empagliflozin-hfpef-hosp.check: same protocol wording; NCT05057806 lists T2D and HFpEF

sglt2-hfref-hosp-cvdeath.check: already declared in the topic config (population_none_entry_condition_only)

colchicine-secondary-cv-prevention.check: Raju 2012 (21918905) enrolled acute coronary syndrome OR acute ischaemic stroke: not a stroke-only population
colchicine-secondary-cv-prevention.deferred_why: the rule is checked (Raju 2012 is not a stroke-only population and would be included), but including it makes the page refuse at the harms gate: Raju reports 'an excess of diarrhoea (X(2) 4.14, P = 0.04)' with no arm counts in its held abstract, its full text is subscription-only (not in PMC) and no registry record was found, so the gastrointestinal harm would be KNOWN_REPORTED_NOT_YET_EXTRACTED. Until Raju's counts are held (or refused on a source), the topic keeps its V1 screening (Raju excluded under X2); this is the V1 state, not a new exclusion.

doac-vte-recurrence.check: here '-only' restricts the SAME condition (VTE) to a subgroup the protocol excludes (cancer-associated VTE), it does not name a comorbidity; lifting it would admit cancer-associated VTE trials
